items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And in the trombone section, we had a trombone player... And we had a fine trumpet player named Jimmy Mitchell

ctx.x: And in the trombone section, we had a trombone player that all I ever knew was Tain! Now, Tain, he couldn't read or write, and he couldn't read music. But if somebody else played it... He was like a computer. If somebody else played... Just like Doc Palmer in Jackson, Mississippi. Tain would listen to somebody else play the lead part, and then from then on he knew it. He played all the leads with the band, in the trombone section, you know.

And we had a fine trumpet player named Jimmy Mitchell; they called him Count. And Parker Berry was one of the trombonists and arrangers. And they had several fine writers writing for the band. It was more or less a territorial band.
